newsitem.title: UK: INTERVIEW-Shire sees marketing buy in time.
newsitem.headline: INTERVIEW-Shire sees marketing buy in time.

text.p: Shire Pharmaceuticals Plc, which earlier announced the acquisition of Pharmavene from the U.S., said on Tuesday other buys would likely follow in due course to boost its marketing presence outside Britain.
"It is unlikely we will start with one man and one car," said finance director Stephen Stamp.
"It is more likely to come through an acquisition, but there is no rush," he told Reuters in a telephone interview.
The Pharmavene acquisition will be financed through an 11.56 million stg placing with institutional investors at 214 pence per share. The placing is fully underwritten by Panmure Gordon.
Shire shares were down 3-1/2 pence at 234 pence in mid-morning trade. "Given the amount of shares we've issued that is pretty good," said Stamp.
Stamp said one of the main attractions of the Pharmavene acquisition was that it would give Shire a foothold in the U.S. and experience in dealing with the Food and Drugs Administration (FDA) there.
The FDA is the authority which decides whether a product can be marketed in the U.S. FDA approval can mean that approval in other counries will follow soon afterwards.

Rather than developing drugs, Pharmavene works on delivering technologies which improve the absorbtion of existing medicines. The Pharmavene buy will help making Shire's drugs become more attractive, said Stamp.
The worlwide market for advanced drug delivery is worth about eight billion dollars and could rise to roughly 18 billion dollars by 2000, Shire said.
